marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q001.takeaway: The urogenital ridge is derived from intermediate mesoderm and separates into a medial genital ridge and lateral nephrogenic cord.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q001.displayText:
The urogenital ridge develops from the intermediate mesoderm.

After the formation of the peritoneal cavity, the intermediate mesoderm is seen as a bulge in the posterior abdominal wall. This bulge lateral to the attachment of the dorsal mesentery is known as the urogenital ridge.

The urogenital ridge has 2 parts:
• The genital ridge, which is medial and gives rise to the genital system
• The nephrogenic cord, which is lateral and contributes to the urinary system

rationales.a: Paraxial mesoderm forms somites and their derivatives; it does not form the urogenital ridge.
rationales.c: Lateral plate mesoderm contributes to body-wall and visceral mesodermal structures, not the urogenital ridge.
rationales.d: Extraembryonic mesoderm lies outside the embryo proper and is not the source of the urogenital ridge.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q002.takeaway: Metanephric blastema forms the nephron excretory segments, whereas the ureteric bud forms the collecting system.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q002.displayText:
The proximal convoluted tubules develop from the metanephric blastema.

The kidney develops from 3 sources as follows:
• Metanephric blastema gives rise to the excretory system of the kidney. It forms the Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, the loop of Henle, and distal convoluted tubule.
• Ureteric bud, which is an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct, gives rise to the collecting system of the kidney. It forms the collecting ducts, minor and major calyces, and renal pelvis.
• Angiogenic mesenchyme, which migrates into the metanephric blastema, gives rise to the glomeruli and the vasa recta.

rationales.a: The mesonephric duct gives rise to the ureteric bud but does not directly form the proximal convoluted tubule.
rationales.c: Mesonephric tubules belong to the transient mesonephric kidney and are not the source of definitive proximal convoluted tubules.
rationales.d: The ureteric bud forms the collecting system, whereas the proximal convoluted tubule is a metanephric-blastema derivative.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q003.takeaway: The ureteric bud sprouts from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct and forms the ureter plus the collecting system of the kidney.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q003.displayText:
The ureteric bud develops from the mesonephric duct (Wolffian duct).

The tip of the ureteric bud penetrates the metanephric blastema, which forms a cap over the distal end of this bud. The ureteric bud gives rise to the ureter and the collecting system of the kidney.

Structures arising from the metanephric blastema and ureteric bud are shown in the source table.

rationales.b: There is no metanephric duct that gives rise to the ureteric bud; the bud arises from the mesonephric duct.
rationales.c: The paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct forms major female reproductive-tract derivatives, not the ureteric bud.
rationales.d: A separate 'ureter duct' is not the embryologic source; the ureter itself is a derivative of the ureteric bud.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q004.takeaway: The source nephron-development sequence is blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped stage → S-shaped stage, corresponding to reconstructed labels 1-4-2-3 (option C).
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q004.displayText: The printed source explanation gives the developmental sequence as blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped (C-shaped) stage → S-shaped stage. The tip of the ureteric bud dilates into an ampulla, which induces adjacent metanephric mesenchyme to epithelialize as a renal vesicle; it then develops through comma-shaped and S-shaped stages. The original question page omits its numbered stage definitions. A contextual reconstruction uses this explicit source sequence and printed key C (1-4-2-3): 1 = blastema stage, 2 = comma-shaped stage, 3 = S-shaped stage, and 4 = vesicle stage. These labels are inferred from the source explanation and key, rather than transcribed from a visible original list. Thus the restored stages give 1-4-2-3. The source sequence includes the comma-shaped stage; it does not substitute a definitive nephron as the fourth listed stage.
emphasis: blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped (C-shaped) stage → S-shaped stage
tip of the ureteric bud dilates into an ampulla

rationales.a: Under the reconstructed legend, 1-2-3-4 puts the vesicle stage last, although vesicle formation precedes comma-shaped and S-shaped stages.
rationales.b: Under the reconstructed legend, 4-3-2-1 starts with the vesicle stage and ends with blastema, reversing the developmental direction.
rationales.d: Under the reconstructed legend, 1-4-3-2 places the S-shaped stage before the comma-shaped stage; comma-shaped development precedes the S-shaped stage.
